synthesis: The Kit User Path map (Filament page /app/kit-user-path, POST /kit-user-path/paths -> KitUserPathController::paths()) currently plots GPS only at scan moments: KitScanPathsQuery reads clarity.kit_scan_paths, a <=15-min ReplacingMergeTree MV of per-kit 15-min scan-path buckets (path_points Array(Tuple), read FINAL), and any bucket with <2 points is dropped -- so the rendered route is fragmented wherever a kit drove without scanning. A prior rebuild attempt (PR #285, discarded) correctly switched the source to clarity.sc_positions (continuous raw GPS) and preserved the response shape, but assembled/segmented the points in PHP with per-point Carbon parsing over the full raw row set, which OOM'd on 'All Kits + 30 days' (~2.3M points -> ~2.2GB / ~7.5s). Dalton's authoritative 'Rebuild guidance' comment mandates redoing the assembly INSIDE ClickHouse (read-only: decimate to 1pt/3s, then groupArray the ordered coords per kit-hour so PHP receives ~one row per kit-hour instead of one row per point, plus a server-side per-segment point cap) so memory stays bounded at any selection width, while keeping HistoricPathBuilder (hour + >500ft-jump segmentation, <2-pt drop) in PHP over the now-small bounded result. This job grounds that decided approach against the current code (it holds up), and produces an implementation-ready scope: a NEW ClickHouse query class (KitScanPathsQuery itself must NOT be touched -- it is shared, unchanged, by two other Scout controllers), a small controller change in KitUserPathController::paths() only, and no client-side change (the PathLayer/tooltip only reads path/color/name; layerId/trip_date are carried through but unused today).

scope.summary: Add a new read-only ClickHouse query class over clarity.sc_positions that decimates to 1pt/3s, groups the ordered coords by (kit_mapping, hour) via groupArray with a server-side per-bucket point cap, and returns a small bounded result; swap KitUserPathController::paths() to resolve selected kit_ids -> lower(kit_mapping) (mirroring ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::kitsByMapping()), call the new query for the fixed [start,end] window, flatten the grouped result back into the flat mapping-tagged point list shape OrgLivePathsQuery::handle() already returns, feed it through the EXISTING OrgLivePathsQuery::segmentByMapping()/HistoricPathBuilder pipeline (no forked segmentation logic), then map kit_mapping back to kit_id/name (KitScanPathsQuery::getColor((int)$kitId) for color parity) to emit the unchanged per-segment response shape {kit_id, name, color, path, layerId, trip_date}. geojson() and hitDensity() on the same controller are untouched -- they read entirely different tables (public_address/public_hotlist_address/hotlist and hits_cold respectively), never kit_scan_paths or sc_positions.

proposed_changes.change: NEW query class. handle(): given lower(kit_mapping) list + [start,end] UTC window, (1) inner subquery: 3s decimation over clarity.sc_positions identical to OrgLivePathsQuery/KitHistoricPositionsQuery (argMin lng/lat by earliest timestamp_utc in each 3s bucket, WHERE lower(kit_mapping) IN (...) AND timestamp_utc BETWEEN start AND end); (2) outer: GROUP BY mapping, toStartOfHour(timestamp_utc), collecting groupArray(tuple(timestamp_utc_string, lng, lat)) per (mapping, hour), arraySort by the timestamp element (groupArray does NOT guarantee input order -- must explicit-sort before applying any cap), then cap array length server-side (private const POINTS_PER_SEGMENT_CAP, proposed default 200, mirrors DECIMATION_SECONDS as a class const, not config). Return array is then flattened in a small handle()-adjacent method into the exact flat shape `list<array{mapping,lng,lat,timestamp_utc}>` that OrgLivePathsQuery::handle() returns, so the controller can call the ALREADY-PUBLIC OrgLivePathsQuery::segmentByMapping($points, $timezone) unchanged -- avoids forking the HistoricPathBuilder-calling logic per the rebuild guidance.
proposed_changes.reason: Read-only CH-side assembly is the mandated fix; keeping the post-flatten shape identical to OrgLivePathsQuery's lets the controller reuse segmentByMapping() (and therefore HistoricPathBuilder) with zero duplicated segmentation logic.

proposed_changes.change: In paths() only: after resolving $kits = KitUsersFilter::format(...), fetch Kit::query()->whereIn('id', $kits)->get() (already org-scoped since $kits came from getUserKits()), build a small private lower(kit_mapping) => Kit map mirroring ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::kitsByMapping() (kits with a null/empty kit_mapping are skipped), call KitRangePathsQuery::query(['mappings' => array_keys($byMapping), 'start' => ..., 'end' => ..., 'cacheTTL' => now()->addMinutes(5)], cache: true) instead of KitScanPathsQuery::query(...), then OrgLivePathsQuery::segmentByMapping($points, $timezone) to get per-mapping segments, then map each mapping's segments back to {kit_id, name: kit->name, color: KitScanPathsQuery::getColor((int)$kit->id), path: segment['path'], layerId: $validated['date_toggles'], trip_date: segment['trip_date']} rows and json-encode the flat list -- byte-identical response DTO shape to today.
proposed_changes.reason: This is the ONLY in-scope controller method per the ticket AC's; geojson()/hitDensity() are confirmed to read unrelated tables.

proposed_changes.change: NEW. RequiresClickhouse; seed clarity.sc_positions (per KitHistoricPositionsQueryTest's insertScPosition convention: geo as string "(lng, lat)", timestamp_utc column) across multiple kit_mappings/hours; assert (a) decimation+grouping produces a bounded row count (rows ~ mappings*hours-with-data, not points), (b) point order within a bucket is chronological despite groupArray's unordered aggregation (arraySort correctness), (c) the per-bucket cap truncates/bounds a dense single-hour bucket without erroring, (d) single-point and zero-point windows degrade to empty/no-segment (AC-5, exercised end-to-end via HistoricPathBuilder's <2-pt drop after flattening), (e) omitting a mapping with no rows in-window returns no rows for it (not an error).

questions.q: Server-side per-segment (kit-hour bucket) point cap: what concrete value, and by what mechanism (naive head-truncation vs even-interval subsampling) when a single kit-hour bucket exceeds it?
questions.answer: Default 200 points/segment as a private class const on the new query class (mirrors KitHistoricPositionsQuery::DECIMATION_SECONDS convention -- not a config value). This is Dalton's own measured value in the rebuild guidance ('groupArray + 200-pt/segment cap: ~4,066 rows, ~750k coords, ~90MB, bounded'), so 200 itself needs no further sign-off. The truncation MECHANISM is a safe engineering default left to implementation: prefer arraySort-then-even-subsample over naive head-truncation so a dense/idle hour (kit sitting still, still ticking every 3s = up to 1200 pts/hour with near-zero displacement, so HistoricPathBuilder would never break it) doesn't get its route visually chopped to only its first ~10 minutes -- this only matters for pathological dense-idle hours; normal selections (single kit / 7d ~8.5k points per Dalton's own numbers) essentially never hit the cap. Safe engineering default, no sign-off needed.

questions.q: Data source: sc_positions vs kit_trips vs kit_scan_paths?
questions.answer: clarity.sc_positions, per Dalton's rebuild guidance -- verified against code (DEV-2018 precedent + kit_trips overlap problem + kit_scan_paths is the current fragmented-route root cause). Not re-opened.
ClickHouse (read-only groupArray), per Dalton's rebuild guidance -- the prior PHP-side attempt (PR #285) OOM'd and was discarded for exactly this reason. Not re-opened.

questions.q: Decimation interval: can it be widened beyond 3s to further reduce payload?
questions.answer: No -- 3s is REQUIRED and must not be widened. HistoricPathBuilder's 500ft break threshold is calibrated for ~3s spacing; widening shreds a moving-vehicle route into dropped single points (this exact failure mode is documented in this user's own memory: 'Decimation-widening breaks HistoricPathBuilder segmentation', DEV-2177 prior investigation). Not re-opened.

questions.q: Should KitScanPathsQuery.php itself be modified (e.g. to add an sc_positions branch) instead of adding a new query class?
questions.answer: No -- confirmed via exhaustive grep that KitScanPathsQuery is shared, unmodified, by ClarityScoutMapController (driver 'today' overlay + livePath fallback) and ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::scanPaths() (admin historical overlay), and this exact 'do not modify, it's shared, add elsewhere' constraint is an established, repeatedly-enforced repo convention (DEV-2185, DEV-2199 build records both state this explicitly). A new query class is required.

questions.q: Do geojson()/hitDensity() on KitUserPathController also read kit_scan_paths and need touching?
questions.answer: No -- read directly: geojson() calls HotlistAddressGeohashQuery (public_address/public_hotlist_address/hotlist tables); hitDensity() calls HitDensityGeohashQuery (hits_cold table). Neither references kit_scan_paths or sc_positions. Confirmed unrelated and untouched.

questions.q: Does the deck.gl PathLayer / tooltip need any per-row field beyond path/color/name, i.e. does the response DTO shape need to change at all?
questions.answer: No JS change needed -- confirmed by reading resources/js/components/kit-user-path.js: renderDataLayer's PathLayer reads only d.path (getPath) and d.color (getColor); the shared tooltip reads only object.object.name. layerId and trip_date are present in the DTO today but not read by any JS in this file. The new response can keep the identical shape.

questions.q: Exact naming for the new query class -- reuse KitRangePathsQuery (the prior discarded attempt's class name) or pick a new name to avoid confusion with the discarded PR's implementation?
questions.answer: KitRangePathsQuery -- reuse the prior name. The old file no longer exists (no conflict), it is descriptive (paths for kits over a fixed [start,end] range), and it is consistent with sibling query-class naming (KitHistoricPositionsQuery / OrgLivePathsQuery).

questions.q: Should the new query class also serve as the fix path for DEV-2222 (kit_scan_paths fallback for scan-only kits), i.e. should paths() try sc_positions first and fall back to the old kit_scan_paths query when a kit has zero sc_positions rows in-window -- or is that strictly DEV-2222's job with zero groundwork laid here?
questions.answer: No groundwork -- strict. Ship only the sc_positions continuous route; scan-only kits (zero sc_positions in-window) render empty exactly as the prior attempt did. DEV-2222 handles the kit_scan_paths fallback entirely on its own. Keeps this PR tight and the DEV-2222 boundary clean.

notes: clarity.kit_scan_paths DDL (database/schema/clickhouse-schema.sql:143): CREATE TABLE clarity.kit_scan_paths (kit_id Int32, org_id Int32, timestamp DateTime, scan_count UInt64, path_points Array(Tuple(Float64,Float64)), kit_name String DEFAULT '', _version DateTime64(3)) ENGINE=ReplacingMergeTree(_version) ... TTL 90 days -- confirms the ticket's 'scan events only, 15-min buckets' description exactly.

groupArray does NOT guarantee element order in ClickHouse (values 'can be added to the array in any order' per CH semantics) -- the new query MUST carry the per-point timestamp into the array and arraySort by it before any cap is applied, or the assembled path can come out visually scrambled. This is an implementation-correctness detail, not a design decision, and is called out explicitly in proposed_changes.

OrgLivePathsQuery::segmentByMapping(array $points, string $timezone) is ALREADY public static and takes exactly the flat `list<array{mapping,lng,lat,timestamp_utc}>` shape -- if the new query's handle() flattens its grouped CH result back into that same shape, the controller can call segmentByMapping() directly and never duplicate the HistoricPathBuilder-calling logic. This directly satisfies the rebuild guidance's 'avoid forking the logic OrgLivePathsQuery/KitHistoricPositionsQuery share.'

Color parity confirmed exact (not just approximate): KitScanPathsQuery's SQL arrayElement(COLORS, (kit_id % 42) + 1) is CH's 1-indexed equivalent of PHP's COLORS[kit_id % 42], which is exactly what KitScanPathsQuery::getColor((int) $kitId) returns (count(self::COLORS) is used dynamically, so parity holds even if the palette size ever changes).

exhaustiveness.idiom: DB::clickhouse($table, $connection='clarity', $final=false, $as=null) (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:69) resolves the clarity. prefix and FINAL keyword based on driver: under the real 'clickhouse' driver it appends ' FINAL' to the table name only (no DB prefix -- the connection itself is already scoped to the clarity database); under the local 'pgsql' bridge driver it prepends a literal 'clarity.' to the table name (and never appends FINAL, since Postgres has no such keyword). Raw whereRaw/selectRaw SQL built directly against DB::clickhouse()'s builder therefore never needs to hand-roll the clarity./FINAL logic -- OrgLivePathsQuery and KitHistoricPositionsQuery both call DB::clickhouse('sc_positions') with no final flag (sc_positions has no ReplacingMergeTree collapse to worry about) and no manual prefix, exactly as the new query class should. ClickhouseQuery::clarityDb()/zodDb() are a SEPARATE idiom used only by classes that need the DB prefix INSIDE a raw cross-database subquery string (e.g. HotlistAddressGeohashQuery's FROM {$zodDb}.public_address) -- not needed here since the new query stays single-table.

AND timestamp_utc BETWEEN ? AND ? GROUP BY mapping, toStartOfInterval(timestamp_utc, INTERVAL 3 SECOND)
